title: A map from a smooth product to an abelian variety is determined by its axes
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $V,W$ be smooth separated geometrically integral finite-type $k$-schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-pc-geometrically-irreducible, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], where separated means the diagonal is a closed immersion. Let $v_0\in V(k)$ and $w_0\in W(k)$ [def-pc-rational-point]. Let $A/k$ be an abelian variety [def-sc-abelian-variety], with identity $0:\operatorname{Spec}k\to A$. Suppose $h:V\times_k W\to A$ is a $k$-morphism [def-pc-fibre-product] whose composites with $V\times\{w_0\}\to V\times_kW$ and $\{v_0\}\times W\to V\times_kW$ are both the constant identity morphism. Then $h$ is the constant identity morphism on $V\times_kW$. Neither $V$ nor $W$ is required to be proper.

source.place: Chapter I Theorem 3.4, printed p.18; the proof uses Lemmas 3.5 and 3.6. Specialization to an algebraically closed ground field and identity value.

proof.text: We first record the geometric hypotheses for the products used below. The product of two smooth $k$-schemes is smooth: its projection is smooth by [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2), and its structure map is smooth by [lem-trf-smooth-composition]. It is of finite type when the factors are, by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]. In particular $V\times_kW$ is reduced by [lem-trf-smooth-geometrically-normal]. An abelian variety is proper, hence separated and of finite type, by [def-sc-abelian-variety] and [def-weil-proper-morphism].

source.place: Chapter I Theorem 3.4 and its proof, printed pp.18–19; Theorem 3.2, Lemmas 3.5–3.6 and Theorem 1.1.

proof.text: The products of separated factors below are separated. Indeed their diagonal, after reordering the four factors, is the product of the two diagonals. Affine-locally its ideal is the sum of the two pulled-back diagonal ideals: the map from the coordinate ring onto the quotient by that sum is surjective. This is precisely the affine-local criterion for a closed immersion in [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Thus the diagonal is closed, as required by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. This argument applies to $V\times_kW$ and to $\overline C\times_kW$ below.

source.place: Chapter I Theorem 3.4 and its proof, printed pp.18–19; Theorem 3.2, Lemmas 3.5–3.6 and Theorem 1.1.

proof.text: Fix a smooth separated geometrically integral pointed curve $(C,c)$ over $k$ and a $k$-morphism $u:C\to V$ with $u(c)=v_0$. Write $h_C=h\circ(u\times\mathrm{id}_W)$. Both of its axis restrictions are zero by the hypotheses on $h$. By [lem-sc-compactification] choose a proper smooth connected curve $j:C\hookrightarrow\overline C$. The point $j(c)$ makes $\overline C$ geometrically connected by [lem-sbc-connected-rational-point-geometrically-connected]. The product $\overline C\times_kW$ is nonempty and connected by [lem-weil-pbc-geometrically-connected-product-components], since $W$ is nonempty and connected. By step 1 it is smooth and of finite type. The geometric regularity in [lem-trf-smooth-geometrically-normal], at the identity field extension, makes it regular; hence [lem-sc-regular-connected-integral] makes it integral. Step 2 makes it separated. The open subscheme $C\times_kW$ is nonempty (it has $(c,w_0)$), so it is dense in this integral product. Apply [lem-sfb-weil-extension-to-abelian-variety] to obtain $\overline h_C:\overline C\times_kW\to A$ extending $h_C$.

source.place: Chapter I Theorem 3.4 and its proof, printed pp.18–19; Theorem 3.2, Lemmas 3.5–3.6 and Theorem 1.1.

proof.text: The curve $\overline C$ itself is regular and integral: it is smooth, nonempty and connected, so [lem-trf-smooth-geometrically-normal] and [lem-sc-regular-connected-integral] apply. Consequently $j(C)$ is dense and $\overline C$ is reduced. The maps $\overline h_C(-,w_0)$ and $0$ agree after $j$, so [lem-sfb-relative-separated-dominant-ext] makes them equal on $\overline C$. Now [lem-sc-rigidity] applies with $X=\overline C$, $Y=W$, $Z=A$, and $y_0=w_0$: $X$ is proper, geometrically connected and geometrically reduced (the latter by [lem-trf-smooth-geometrically-normal]), $W$ is connected, and $A$ is separated and of finite type. It gives $\overline h_C=g\circ\operatorname{pr}_W$. Restricting along $\{j(c)\}\times W$ gives $g=0$, because that restriction lies in $C\times W$ and equals $h(v_0,-)=0$. Therefore $h_C=0$.

source.place: Chapter I Theorem 3.4 and its proof, printed pp.18–19; Theorem 3.2, Lemmas 3.5–3.6 and Theorem 1.1.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-pointed-curves-dense] to $(V,v_0)$ and obtain $(C_i,c_i,u_i)_{i\in I}$ with dense union of images. Fix $w\in W(k)$ and put $h_w=h(-,w):V\to A$. Step 4 gives $h_wu_i=0$ for every $i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], the maps $u_i$ assemble to a map $u:\coprod_i C_i\to V$; its image is the dense union just obtained. The same universal property shows $h_wu=0u$, since the composites agree on every summand. The source $V$ is reduced (it is integral), and $A$ is separated over $k$. Thus [lem-sfb-relative-separated-dominant-ext] gives $h_w=0$ as a morphism of schemes. This holds for every $w\in W(k)$.

source.place: Chapter I Theorem 3.4 and its proof, printed pp.18–19; Theorem 3.2, Lemmas 3.5–3.6 and Theorem 1.1.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-rational-points-dense] to the smooth scheme $V\times_kW$ of step 1: its $k$-rational points are dense. Each such point is a pair $(v,w)$ by the defining property of the fibre product, and step 5 gives equality of the two $k$-morphisms from $\operatorname{Spec}k$ obtained by evaluating $h$ and $0$ at $(v,w)$. Form the coproduct of $\operatorname{Spec}k$ over this set of rational points, using [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], and its evaluation map $e$ to $V\times_kW$. Its image is dense, and $he=0e$ by the coproduct universal property. Since $V\times_kW$ is reduced by step 1 and $A$ is separated over $k$, [lem-sfb-relative-separated-dominant-ext] yields $h=0$. This proves equality as morphisms, including their structure-sheaf maps.

Smooth schemes are geometrically regular and reduced; this is a generic source-hypothesis check, not a trace-formula step.
The generic rational-section criterion verifies geometric connectedness of the compactified curve.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q75-6849f50ed (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, the new node, every cited statement and the source in full; review.md has the step-by-step checks. Source: Milne AV I.3.4 with Lemmas 3.5 and 3.6 (printed pp.18-19). The item statement is unchanged, is the a0=0, k=k̄ case of Thm 3.4, and is not weakened. The six steps follow Milne's route and I checked each cited node's hypotheses at its step. Step 1: smooth under base change and composition, finite type, reduced. Step 2 is elementary and I accept it: a product of separated schemes has diagonal Δ×Δ, which is affine-locally I⊗B+A⊗J. Step 3: compactify C. C̄ is geometrically connected because j(c) is a k-point. C̄×W is connected by the component bijection and integral because it is regular and connected. C×W is a dense open containing (c,w0), so Weil extension applies to an integral, separated, finite-type, smooth source. Step 4: C̄ is reduced and dense-image equality gives h̄_C(-,w0)=0. All hypotheses of lem-sc-rigidity hold (C̄ proper, geometrically connected and geometrically reduced; W connected; A separated and locally of finite type), and restricting along j(c) gives g=h(v0,-)=0. Step 5: the new node and an arbitrary-index coproduct give a dense image in the reduced V, so h_w=0. Step 6: k-points of V×W are dense and V×W is reduced, so h=0 as a morphism. The new node lem-sfb-smooth-pointed-curves-dense is true: normalization of an irreducible curve through x0 is a smooth curve with a point over x0 and the same image, which is Milne 3.6 with 3.5(b). I tested it on X a point (constant map from A¹), a curve, and Aⁿ. It is statement-only, self-contained, and its definitions are cited. Scanning all node statements found no duplicate. It is not a restatement of the item, and no existing node already states the item (relative-abelian-pointed-rigidity and sc-rigidity both need properness). Batch 5: lem-trf-smooth-composition and lem-trf-smooth-geometrically-normal are general smoothness facts, and weil-extension reaches the trace-formula chapter only through the second of them. None of these is part of the trace formula or Poincaré duality or their proofs, so I accept them as generic tools; the two trf nodes are recorded in tool_uses. No changes.
